articles.dek: Journalists are essential for making sense of crises, countering misinformation and giving communities a voice. They need protection and support, especially local and independent ones, because informed citizens and meaningful participation depend on reliable, diverse news.

articles.title: WORLD NEWS DAY OP-ED: Journalism and our chaotic world’s future
articles.dek: Journalism faces growing pressure from governments, powerful technology companies and its own crisis of trust, making control over information an increasingly important struggle for power. Its survival depends on rebuilding public trust through independent, transparent and accountable reporting while adapting to new technologies without abandoning its purpose.

articles.title: WORLD NEWS DAY OP-ED: India’s students found their voice this summer while journalists are losing theirs
articles.dek: India’s press freedom is increasingly being exercised by citizens, students, influencers, and comedians who challenge power online. But true press freedom requires independent journalism that can survive without censorship, government pressure, surveillance or financial dependence.

articles.title: The tech battle to build your AI assistant
articles.dek: The long-promised personal AI assistant is finally arriving, with a suddenly crowded field of agents offering to run pieces of your everyday life. Why it matters: For years, tech's "personal assistants" were little more than voice-controlled search boxes. Rapid advances in AI are finally giving them the memory, judgment and autonomy to act on our behalf. Catch up quick: Chatbots answer questions.
